config.subtitle: Quick answers about Berlin Then and Now, my walking tour through the old city.

items.q: How long is the walking tour?
items.a: About **2.5 hours and about 3 km** on foot. The route is mostly flat, and every stop has time for the archive photo, your questions and a short breather before the next part of the city.

items.q: Where does the walking tour start and end?
items.a: We start at 12:30 at the **World Clock (Weltzeituhr) on Alexanderplatz**, the rotating globe in the middle of the square. The walk ends at **Hackescher Markt**, with food, coffee and the S-Bahn right there.

items.q: How much does the walk cost?
items.a: **€25 per person, paid when you book.** Cancel up to 24 hours before the start and you get a full refund, or move to another date if there is space. Later than that I cannot refund.

items.q: What will I see on the walk?
items.a: **11 stops covering 16 places** in Berlin's oldest quarter: the World Clock, the TV Tower, the Rotes Rathaus and the Neptune Fountain, St. Mary's Church, the Marx-Engels-Forum, the Sanchi Gate, the Humboldt Forum, the Lustgarten with the Berliner Dom and the Altes Museum, the Neues Museum, the Alte Nationalgalerie and the Pergamon, the Friedrichsbrücke and Hackescher Markt. At every stop I hold up an archive photo of the same place.

items.q: Do I need to book the walking tour in advance?
items.a: **Yes, book your date online** at walkofberlin.com. The group is no more than 10 people, and a walk needs at least 2 guests. If you are the only guest one hour before the start, I cancel the walk, refund you in full and give you one of my audio walks for free.
